transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-23 16:00 PT
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Morales (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (SE), Maya Chen (Head of ML, CinderPoint), Tom Rivers (VP Eng), Ibrahim Osei (FinOps)

Summary: (auto) Quick QBR-style workshop — review last quarter usage, discuss cost spikes on embeddings, talk about reliability incidents during peak, align on pilot to validate Dedicated capacity for lower p99 latency.

00:00 Jenna Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call, uh, and we'll jump into usage.
00:18 Maya Chen: Hey Jenna, hi Ravi. Glad we could do this, we've got Tom and Ibrahim on — I'll hand over to Tom for a sec to give context on engineering priorities.
00:27 Tom Rivers: Hi all. Our big thing this quarter is stabilizing the customer conversation flow — we've had a couple of p99 blips and some cost surprises on embeddings. We want to validate a setup that gets us under 250ms median generation for short chat, and bring embedding unit cost down about 20%.
00:45 Jenna Morales: Got it. Ibrahim, from FinOps any red flags we should call out up front?
00:53 Ibrahim Osei: Yeah, mainly we need a forecast that's tied to a pilot. We can't sign a Dedicated commitment without a clearer burn model — last month's bill was 30% over our estimate.
01:08 Ravi Patel: Ok, quick framing: we'll cover token mix, batching/quantization levers, cache hit expectations, then propose a pilot test plan.
01:20 Maya Chen: Sounds good.

05:10 Ravi Patel: So looking at the data you sent, CinderPoint is ~65% embeddings by call volume, but embeddings only consume ~20% of token spend — it's the frequent short chats with long contexts that drive token count. Also noticed prefix caching was off on a lot of routes. Might be misconfigured on the SDK side.
05:40 Tom Rivers: We did a quick SDK upgrade last month, maybe that's the cause. The SDK started reattaching full context instead of relying on K-V cache — I think the transcriber wrote that as K-V cash in our notes, ha.
06:05 Ravi Patel: Totally. If the client is re-sending full history, that explains both the cost jump and the latency increase under load. We can provide a hotfix snippet; it's low effort but has big impact.

10:15 Maya Chen: On reliability, we had two incidents in May where p95 climbed to 1.4s for inference on hosted endpoints during a peak ETL job. The errors were transient but impacted customer-facing dialogue.
10:36 Jenna Morales: Did those line up with autoscaling or was it capacity throttling?
10:45 Ravi Patel: Looks like a combination: your traffic pattern had a sudden concurrency burst and our autoscaler for your region was slow to spin; also the model variant they fell back to had a cold KV cache.
11:03 Tom Rivers: Is that something Dedicated would help with? We were hoping Dedicated gives predictable p99.
11:11 Ravi Patel: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbors and gives headroom, but you still need caching and warmup strategies for p99. For real tail latency improvement we'll suggest a canary with pre-warmed KV caches and a small steady baseline.

15:00 Ibrahim Osei: Budget question — how should we think about cost sensitivity between Hosted vs Dedicated? Our CFO wants a per-user/unit estimate not just token rates.
15:18 Jenna Morales: We'll send a pilot pricing sheet but practically, Dedicated offers lower per-token cost at higher committed spend; hosted is pay-as-you-go but spikes can surprise you. We can model three scenarios: conservative, expected, and growth.
15:40 Ravi Patel: Also quantization profiles matter. For your 8k context model, a 4-bit quantized variant can lower GPU utilization ~22-28% in our tests, tradeoff around some generation variability. We can run a quality guardrail eval on your prompt set.

22:05 Maya Chen: We care a lot about quality delta — many of our responses are compliance-adjacent so hallucination tolerances are low. Any change we make, we need a scorecard.
22:20 Ravi Patel: Totally — propose we run an A/B on 500 prompts from you, measure rouge-ish and failure modes, plus human spot checks and our automatic regression alerts.
22:41 Tom Rivers: How long for the benchmark? We need to align calendar-wise.
22:48 Jenna Morales: We can do bench runs in 48–72 hours once we have the traffic trace and prompt set, but end-to-end with analysis ~7 business days.

28:12 Ravi Patel: On SLOs — you're looking for 99.9% availability and p95 under 500ms for small chat. For Dedicated we can map SLOs with an SLA addendum; for Hosted we'd propose routing policies (region, capacity tier) and fallbacks.
28:40 Maya Chen: Do you have audit logs for who called endpoints and content retention controls?
28:47 Jenna Morales: Yes — Redwood stores audit logs and offers retention windows; we also support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. I think you asked about SOC 2 earlier?
28:58 Ibrahim Osei: Right — SOC 2, and also ISO piece — we'll need SOC docs and a quick security one-pager for procurement.
29:06 Jenna Morales: We'll send SOC 2 and a short security FAQ.

33:30 Tom Rivers: Back to cost optimizations — Ravi, you mentioned caching — what are expected hit rates with the typical conversational workload?
33:44 Ravi Patel: For conversational routes with stable prompts we see 40–65% prefix cache hits after a warm period. If your app replays full history every time it's much lower. With the SDK fix and a small warm baseline we should hit mid-50s.
34:02 Maya Chen: Is there a config we can set to prefer prefix reuse?
34:08 Ravi Patel: Yes, it's an SDK flag plus a platform route hint. We'll include the snippet in the follow-up.

40:10 Ibrahim Osei: About the pilot — finance wants a 12-week pilot that maps to clear gates: 1) performance validation, 2) cost pairing, 3) reliability under simulated peak. We need milestone metrics.
40:28 Jenna Morales: Proposed pilot: 6 weeks active bench + 6 weeks soft live traffic on Dedicated reserved pool. Gates: median latency <300ms, p99 improved >30% vs hosted baseline, and embedding cost down 15% from current. If you pass gates we scope a 12-month commit.
40:56 Tom Rivers: We might compress to 8 weeks total if benchmarks go well — but let's keep conservative planning.

46:15 Maya Chen: A few product questions — do you support deterministic reranking and reranker caching (we have heavy rerank workloads)?
46:26 Ravi Patel: Rerank caching is doable for top-K stable queries; determinism depends on model sampling settings — we'll recommend deterministic in rerank passes and show you the config.

52:05 Jenna Morales: Ok recap: Redwood action — send pilot pricing, security docs, SDK snippet for cache, and schedule the performance benchmark. CinderPoint action — share prompt set + traffic, Ibrahim to confirm budget owner, Tom and Maya confirm pilot dates.
52:30 Maya Chen: Yep, I'll package the prompts tonight and share.
52:40 Ibrahim Osei: I'll talk to finance and confirm by Monday.
52:47 Tom Rivers: I'll coordinate engineering availability for the benchmark window in early July.

60:00 Jenna Morales: Thanks all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 90-minute benchmark and circulate the pilot doc.
60:12 Maya Chen: Thanks, bye.
60:20 Ravi Patel: Thanks everyone.
